name: comp_comm_pipe_create
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Pipes are the canonical parent-child IPC primitive and underpin shell pipelines, subprocess stdio, and many command-line patterns; modeling them lets the substrate represent unix pipelines as first-class card compositions.
semantics: Allocate a unidirectional kernel buffer with two endpoints: one read-only handle and one write-only handle. Bytes written to the write end are buffered (default PIPE_BUF = 4KiB on Linux, larger on macOS) and become available on the read end in FIFO order. The pipe is anonymous by default; named pipes (FIFOs / mkfifo) are a separate primitive. Pipes are the classical parent-child IPC channel: fork inherits both ends, then each side closes the unused end. flags may include O_NONBLOCK and O_CLOEXEC on POSIX; Windows CreatePipe takes a SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES + buffer-size pair.

name: comp_comm_shared_memory
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Shared memory is the lowest-latency IPC primitive and underpins zero-copy ring buffers, lock-free queues, and large-tensor handoff; the substrate must model both POSIX and System V flavors plus the iOS refusal to keep cross-platform contracts honest.
semantics: Create or open a named shared-memory segment and map it into the calling process's address space, yielding a pointer through which multiple processes can read and write the same physical pages. POSIX flavour: shm_open + ftruncate + mmap(MAP_SHARED). System V flavour: shmget + shmat. The returned region_handle owns the kernel-side object; mapped_ptr is the user-space view. Synchronization across the shared region is the caller's responsibility (semaphores, mutexes in shared memory, atomic operations). On unmap/release the kernel-side object persists until shm_unlink / IPC_RMID is invoked by an owning process.
signature: (name: str, size: usize, flags: u32, mode: u32) -> (region_handle, mapped_ptr: ptr<u8>) | error

name: comp_comm_socket_connect

semantics: Initiate a connection from the local socket to a remote endpoint described by 'addr'. name: comp_comm_socket_send_recv
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Send/recv is the data-plane primitive of all socket-based protocols; modeling it once lets RPC, HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC cards share a single emit path.

name: comp_compute_parallel_map
rationale: W47 substrate population for the 'compute' computation category. Parallel-map sits alongside sequential map but explicitly commits to concurrent execution, which the substrate's optimizer treats as a distinct cost model. Cilk's work-stealing scheduler is the canonical realization; Rayon and TBB are direct descendants.
semantics: Applies a pure function f to every element of xs concurrently, producing a result collection of the same length and order. Distinct from comp_compute_map_over_collection in that this primitive explicitly commits to parallel execution: the runtime is expected to partition xs across worker threads (typically using work-stealing as in Cilk / Rayon / TBB) and may dynamically rebalance load. Element order in the result is preserved (output[i] = f(xs[i])) even though evaluation order is concurrent. f must be data-race-free (pure functions trivially satisfy this). Throws no exceptions if f is total; if f panics on some element, the parallel map propagates the first panic deterministically.

name: comp_compute_reduce_collection
rationale: W47 substrate population for the 'compute' computation category. Reduce is the second of the three fundamental higher-order collection operations. The substrate needs reduce as a first-class primitive so that aggregation contracts (sum, product, fold) are expressible without picking a backend strategy.
semantics: Folds (reduces) a collection xs into a single accumulated value by repeatedly applying a pure binary function f, starting from an initial accumulator value init. When f is associative (e.g. integer addition, string concatenation, max/min), the runtime may parallelize the reduction tree; the primitive does not commit to an evaluation order at the spec level but downstream optimizer cards may exploit associativity. Output element type may differ from input element type via the binary function's signature.

name: comp_cm_lambda_beta_reduce
rationale: W47 substrate population for the 'compute_model' computation category. The lambda calculus is the functional counterpart to the Turing machine; beta-reduction is its atomic step. The substrate needs this card to express functional-evaluation semantics formally and to ground type-theory cards (Pierce TAPL) that build on it.
semantics: Performs one beta-reduction step on a lambda term. Beta-reduction rewrites a redex of the form ((λx. body) arg) to body[x := arg], i.e. substitutes arg for every free occurrence of x in body, alpha-renaming bound variables as needed to avoid variable capture. This is the atomic computation step of the untyped lambda calculus and forms the foundation of functional programming languages. Evaluation strategies that build on this primitive include normal-order (leftmost-outermost), applicative-order (leftmost-innermost), call-by-name, call-by-value, and call-by-need (lazy). By Church's theorem the lambda calculus is Turing-complete; every computable function has a corresponding lambda term.

name: comp_cm_pi_calculus_message
rationale: W47 substrate population for the 'compute_model' computation category. The pi-calculus is the foundational model of concurrent computation with channel mobility; Milner's calculus underlies modern session-types, capability security, and distributed systems theory. The substrate needs this card to ground concurrency / communication cards in a formal model. Abadi & Cardelli's calculus of mobile objects builds on pi-calculus.
semantics: Performs the atomic communication step of the pi-calculus (Milner, Parrow, Walker 1992): a synchronous message exchange between two processes over a shared channel name. The send_process has the form (c!v . P) — send value v on channel c then continue as P. The recv_process has the form (c?x . Q) — receive on channel c, bind to x, then continue as Q. The communication step rewrites the parallel composition (c!v . P) | (c?x . Q) to P | Q[x := v]. Channel names are first-class values that can themselves be sent (mobility) — this is what distinguishes pi-calculus from CCS and gives it the expressive power to model dynamic process networks, object-oriented method dispatch, and capability-based security. Foundational model for concurrent computation.
signature: (send_process: pi_process, recv_process: pi_process, channel: channel_name, value: pi_value) -> (pi_process_continuation, pi_process_continuation)

name: comp_cm_recursive_call
rationale: W47 substrate population for the 'compute_model' computation category. General recursion is the third foundational model alongside Turing machines and lambda calculus; Kleene's mu-recursive functions formalized this. The substrate needs this primitive because most real programming languages express computation via recursion + iteration rather than tape transitions or beta reduction.
semantics: Performs a recursive function call in the general-recursion model of computation. The call_stack is the explicit activation record stack: pushing a new frame containing (return_address, local_bindings, args) onto call_stack; evaluating f's body in that environment; popping the frame on return. General recursion (as opposed to primitive recursion) allows the function to call itself unrestricted, so termination is not guaranteed in general — this is what makes the model Turing-complete. The primitive includes tail-call recognition: when the recursive call is in tail position, the implementation may reuse the current frame (tail-call optimization, TCO) producing iteration with bounded stack depth. Otherwise stack grows by one frame per call until base case or stack overflow.

name: comp_cm_register_machine_step
rationale: W47 substrate population for the 'compute_model' computation category. The register machine is the bridge between abstract models (Turing, lambda) and real hardware (rv32i, arm64). The substrate needs this card so that its codegen contracts (comp_compile_emit_target) have a formal model of the machine they target.
semantics: Executes one instruction of a RISC-style register machine. A state is (program_counter, register_file, memory). The instruction at memory[program_counter] is decoded into (opcode, operands) and executed: register reads, ALU computation, register write, then program_counter advance (or jump for branch instructions). Instruction set is RISC: load, store, alu (add, sub, mul, div, and, or, xor, shl, shr), branch (beq, bne, blt, bge), jump, call/return. Each step is constant-time on idealized hardware. This is the abstract model of which real CPUs (rv32i, arm64, x86_64) are concrete realizations; it is also the canonical compilation target for higher-level compute models.

name: comp_cm_turing_step
rationale: W47 substrate population for the 'compute_model' computation category. The Turing machine is the foundational abstract model of computation; its single-step primitive is the atom of every computability proof. The substrate needs this card to express decidability/complexity claims and to ground other compute models via cross-simulation.
semantics: Executes a single transition of a Turing machine. A configuration is the tuple (state, tape, head_position). The transition function delta : (state, tape_symbol) -> (state', tape_symbol', head_move) maps the current state and symbol-under-head to: new state, symbol to write, head direction (L | R | N). If the configuration's state is the halting state, the step returns halted; otherwise it returns a new configuration with the updated state, tape (with one cell rewritten), and head shifted by one. This is the atomic step of universal computation per Turing's 1936 model; sufficient to express any computable function (Church-Turing thesis).

name: comp_crypto_aead_decrypt
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. The dual of comp_crypto_aead_encrypt. RFC 8439 + RFC 5116 specify the release-on-success discipline that this card enforces at the IR level.
semantics: Authenticated decryption verifying the Poly1305 tag in the sealed_box against the (key, nonce, ciphertext, associated_data) tuple. On tag verification success returns the plaintext; on failure returns aead_auth_failure WITHOUT releasing any plaintext bytes (release-on-success discipline mandatory per RFC 5116 §2.2). The associated_data must match the value used at encrypt time bit-for-bit. The primitive is target-agnostic: it describes the WHAT of AEAD-Open; the HOW (constant-time tag comparison to prevent timing oracles, SIMD acceleration, scrubbing the plaintext buffer on auth failure) is the backend executor's responsibility.

name: comp_crypto_aead_encrypt
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. AEAD is the modern baseline for confidentiality+integrity (TLS 1.3 mandatory cipher suite, age-encryption, WireGuard). RFC 8439 + RFC 5116 define the substrate-agnostic interface this card captures.
semantics: Authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD), defaulting to ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) with a 256-bit key and 96-bit nonce. The nonce MUST be unique per (key, message) pair; reuse catastrophically breaks confidentiality and forgery resistance. The primitive is target-agnostic: it describes the WHAT of AEAD-Seal; the HOW (ChaCha20-Poly1305 vs AES-GCM negotiation, SIMD acceleration, constant-time discipline) is the backend executor's responsibility. A future card may parameterize the AEAD construction (AES-GCM, XChaCha20-Poly1305).

name: comp_crypto_sign_ed25519
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Ed25519 (RFC 8032, NIST SP 800-186) is the modern baseline asymmetric-signature primitive (SSH, age, signify, the Noise Protocol Framework). This card supplies the substrate-level form.
semantics: Compute an Ed25519 signature (RFC 8032) over message under the 32-byte private key (referenced as a token to avoid leaking key material through the IR). Returns a 64-byte signature (R || S in little-endian Edwards curve encoding). Ed25519 is deterministic: the same (private_key, message) tuple always produces the same signature; no random nonce input is required, and the substrate enforces this by NOT accepting a nonce parameter. The primitive is target-agnostic: it describes the WHAT of Ed25519-Sign; the HOW (libsodium vs OpenSSL vs CryptoKit, constant-time scalar multiplication, side-channel hardening) is the backend executor's responsibility.

name: comp_crypto_verify_ed25519
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. The dual of comp_crypto_sign_ed25519. RFC 8032 specifies the canonical-encoding and small-subgroup-rejection rules this card encodes at the IR level.
semantics: Verify an Ed25519 signature (RFC 8032) over message under public_key. Returns verification_outcome ∈ {accepted, rejected}. The implementation MUST reject non-canonical point encodings and small-subgroup signatures (per RFC 8032 §5.1.7 and ZIP-215 conventions where applicable). The primitive is target-agnostic: it describes the WHAT of Ed25519-Verify; the HOW (batch verification, cofactored vs uncofactored equation, ZIP-215 strictness) is the backend executor's responsibility.

name: comp_gfx_cmd_copy_resource
semantics: Records a GPU-side copy from a source resource to a destination resource into the open command buffer. The copy direction is selected implicitly from (src,dst) types: buffer->buffer is a byte-range copy; buffer->texture and texture->buffer are linearization/delinearization copies with an implicit memory layout (row pitch / array slice / mip level read from region); texture->texture is a sub-rectangle blit. When region is none, the primitive copies the entire src to dst and requires the two resources to have compatible footprints (same size for buffers; same dimensions/format-block for textures). The primitive touches command-buffer state only; the actual DMA executes when the cmdbuf is submitted. Source and destination must be in copy-compatible resource states (transitioned via comp_gfx_cmd_resource_barrier if explicit barriers are required by the target API). Backend executors realize it by emitting the API's blit / copy entry — D3D12 CopyResource/CopyBufferRegion/CopyTextureRegion, Vulkan vkCmdCopyBuffer/vkCmdCopyImage/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage, Metal MTLBlitCommandEncoder.copy.

barrier_state_taxonomy_partial: resource-state and pipeline-stage bitmask enumerations declared abstractly; full enumeration mapping (D3D12 enhanced barrier layout enum, Vulkan VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_* full set, Metal MTLRenderStages exact mapping) deferred to a richer descendant card
name: comp_gfx_cmd_resource_barrier
semantics: Records a synchronization edge into the command buffer that ensures all GPU work in before_stage that uses resource in before_state has fully completed and its writes are visible before any subsequent work in after_stage starts that uses the resource in after_state. The barrier covers three kinds: transition barriers change a resource between usage modes (e.g. render_target -> shader_resource, copy_dst -> shader_resource); uav_aliasing barriers serialize writes through unordered-access views to the same memory; global_memory barriers (resource=none) flush all caches between pipeline stages with no resource scoping. before_state/after_state are bitmasks of resource-state flags (render_target, shader_resource, copy_src, copy_dst, depth_write, depth_read, indirect_arg, present, etc.). before_stage/after_stage are bitmasks of pipeline stages (top, vertex_shader, fragment_shader, compute_shader, color_attachment_output, transfer, bottom). The primitive touches command-buffer state only; the actual execution barrier is emitted when the GPU consumes the cmdbuf. Backend executors realize it via Vulkan vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 (with VkMemoryBarrier2/VkBufferMemoryBarrier2/VkImageMemoryBarrier2 entries) or D3D12 ResourceBarrier (with D3D12_RESOURCE_BARRIER_TYPE_TRANSITION/UAV/ALIASING entries) or Metal MTLFence/MTLEvent (Metal makes most barriers implicit per-encoder; explicit barriers needed only for cross-encoder hazards).

The substrate maps Vulkan onto this primitive via VkDescriptorPool (heap_kind groups by descriptor-type pool sizes); D3D12 maps directly to ID3D12DescriptorHeap; Metal maps to MTLBuffer-backed argument-buffer storage allocated with the device. name: comp_gfx_descriptor_table_layout
semantics: Declares the binding layout of one descriptor table / argument buffer / descriptor set: an ordered list of typed binding ranges, each occupying a contiguous block of slots. Each range carries: kind (the resource type that lives at those slots — CBV/SRV/UAV/sampler in D3D12 terms, sampled_image/storage_buffer/etc. in Vulkan terms), base_slot (the first slot the range covers), count (how many slots; UINT32_MAX means runtime-sized / unbounded for bindless), shader_stage_visibility (which shader stages can read those slots), and flags (e.g. update_after_bind for bindless tables, partially_bound for sparsely populated tables, variable_descriptor_count for the last range). The result is an immutable handle that comp_gfx_pipeline_state_create consumes as part of its render_state and comp_gfx_descriptor_heap_create / comp_gfx_cmd_bind_resources can allocate against. The primitive touches device descriptor-layout state but does not allocate descriptor memory itself. Backend executors realize it by creating the equivalent layout object on the target API. This is the substrate's bindless-capable descriptor-binding declaration primitive — without it, only the small-binding model in comp_gfx_cmd_bind_resources is supported.

name: comp_gfx_device_create
semantics: Acquires an opaque handle to a GPU device addressed by adapter_index (0 == default/primary adapter). The handle is the root factory from which queues, buffers, textures, shaders, and pipelines are spawned; it owns no command state of its own. The primitive touches the platform's driver-side device-enumeration state, allocating internal driver structures for the lifetime of the handle. Backend executors realize this by instantiating the underlying device object on each target's actual GPU API. Failure modes include the requested adapter not existing, the adapter being lost, or the system being out of device memory.

name: comp_gfx_pipeline_state_create
semantics: Bakes a complete pipeline-state object from a set of compiled shader stages plus a render-state card (vertex input layout, primitive topology, rasterizer state, blend state, depth-stencil state, color/depth attachment formats for graphics; or workgroup-size hints and binding layout for compute). The result is an immutable handle that the command recorder binds before issuing draws or dispatches. The primitive triggers driver-side state validation and PSO compilation, often the dominant cost of first-frame hitching. Backend executors realize it by invoking the API's pipeline-creation entry point; cached PSOs should be reused.

name: comp_gfx_present_mode_select
semantics: Switches the swap chain's frame-pacing strategy at runtime without recreating the swapchain (where supported by the backend). present_mode selects: immediate — back buffer flips as soon as it is ready, may tear, lowest latency, tracks the GPU's actual render rate (uncapped FPS); fifo — first-in-first-out queue presents in vsync intervals, no tearing, may stall the CPU/GPU when the queue fills, traditional vsync; fifo_relaxed — same as fifo but tears if the previous frame missed vsync (adaptive vsync), lower judder; mailbox — triple-buffered single-frame-deep queue that always presents the most recent ready frame at vsync (low-latency vsync, no tearing, no CPU/GPU stall). sync_interval is a refinement primarily used on DXGI: 0 = present immediately (used with allow_tearing flag), 1 = wait for one vsync (traditional), >1 = wait for N vsyncs (half-rate / quarter-rate). The primitive touches swapchain state. Backend executors realize it via the target API's runtime present-mode switch. On targets that require swapchain recreation to change present mode (some Vulkan drivers), the primitive triggers a swapchain rebuild internally. On Metal, this maps to CAMetalLayer.displaySyncEnabled and per-drawable presentDrawable(afterMinimumDuration:).

name: comp_gfx_query_perf_counter
semantics: Single-primitive interface to GPU performance counters and queries. op=create_pool allocates a query pool of count entries of query_kind, returns a gfx_query_pool_t. op=begin_query / end_query brackets a recorded GPU work region with an occlusion or pipeline-stats counter that accumulates while the bracket is open. op=write_timestamp records a single GPU timestamp at the current pipeline stage into pool[query_index] (the canonical primitive for measuring GPU frame time — pair two timestamps before/after a workload and read the delta). op=resolve_results reads back count consecutive query values starting at query_index from pool, returns a list of u64 raw counter values (timestamps in device ticks; occlusion as sample count; pipeline_stats as per-stage struct serialized as u64 array). op=destroy_pool releases the pool. timestamp counter frequency / period is queryable per-device (separate device-property primitive). The primitive touches command-buffer state when op is a record-side op, and host memory when op=resolve_results. Backend executors realize each op against the target API's query/counter API. counter_set is the GPU-specific hardware-counter set (AMD GPA, NVIDIA PerfKit, Intel Metrics Discovery on PC; Apple Metal performance counters on Apple Silicon) — substrate exposes them via a unified enum but the value semantics are target-dependent.
signature: (device: gfx_device_t, cmdbuf: gfx_cmdbuf_t|none, op: enum{create_pool,begin_query,end_query,write_timestamp,resolve_results,destroy_pool}, pool: gfx_query_pool_t|none, query_kind: enum{timestamp,occlusion,pipeline_stats,gpu_time_elapsed,counter_set}, query_index: u32|none, count: u32|none) -> u64 | list[u64] | gfx_query_pool_t | ()

name: comp_gfx_resource_destroy
semantics: Releases an opaque GPU resource handle (gfx_buffer_t, gfx_texture_t, gfx_shader_t, gfx_pipeline_t, gfx_queue_t, gfx_device_t, gfx_cmdbuf_t) back to its parent device or the system. The handle is logically invalid after this call. The primitive touches the device allocator and any in-flight reference-tracking state; backends with deferred destruction (Vulkan, D3D12) may queue the release behind outstanding GPU work. Backend executors realize it by calling the API-specific destroy entry point or decrementing the API's reference count. The card itself does not enforce in-flight safety; that contract belongs to higher-level scheduling cards.

name: comp_gfx_root_signature_layout
semantics: Declares the complete top-level binding layout that connects a CPU command-recording surface to a shader's resource-binding view: the root signature (D3D12) / argument-buffer-set layout (Metal) / pipeline-layout (Vulkan). Each parameter is a root-level binding slot of one kind: root_constants directly inlines num_32bit_values uint32 values into the command buffer (fastest, smallest); root_cbv/root_srv/root_uav inlines a single resource virtual-address into the command buffer (one descriptor, no indirection); descriptor_table indirects through a comp_gfx_descriptor_table_layout (full descriptor-table, supports arrays and bindless); sampler_table is a descriptor_table restricted to sampler descriptors (D3D12 mandates samplers live in their own heap). static_samplers are immutable samplers baked into the root signature itself (no descriptor heap slot consumed). flags carry options like ALLOW_INPUT_ASSEMBLER_INPUT_LAYOUT, DENY_*_SHADER_ROOT_ACCESS to prune unused stages, CBV_SRV_UAV_HEAP_DIRECTLY_INDEXED (D3D12 shader-model-6.6 dynamic resources / bindless without an explicit table). The result is an immutable handle that comp_gfx_pipeline_state_create consumes as the pipeline's binding-layout. The primitive touches device pipeline-layout state. Backend executors realize it on the target API; D3D12 maps 1:1, Vulkan maps to vkCreatePipelineLayout over a sequence of VkDescriptorSetLayout (one per descriptor_table parameter) plus VkPushConstantRange (for root_constants), Metal maps to an argument-buffer-set layout where each root parameter becomes one argument buffer or a push-constant slot.
signature: (device: gfx_device_t, parameters: list[(kind: enum{root_constants,root_cbv,root_srv,root_uav,descriptor_table,sampler_table}, slot: u32, descriptor_table_layout: gfx_descriptor_table_layout_t|none, num_32bit_values: u32|none, shader_stage_visibility: bitmask)], static_samplers: list[gfx_static_sampler_desc_t], flags: bitmask) -> gfx_root_signature_t

name: comp_gfx_shader_module_create
semantics: Compiles a card-native shader IR graph (referenced by shader_ir_card_ref into cards/computation/shader_lang/) for a specific pipeline stage on the given device. The shader IR is the substrate's target-agnostic representation, lowered by each backend executor into the target's chip-specific bytecode. The primitive touches the device's shader-cache and may trigger driver-side compilation, which can be expensive on first use; backends should cache compiled artifacts. Backend executors realize it by calling the API's shader-module / library / DXIL creation entry point on bytecode emitted from the IR. Failures include malformed IR, stage capabilities not supported by the device, and compiler-internal errors.

name: comp_gfx_submit_and_present
semantics: Submits cmdbuf to the GPU on queue and, after its work completes, presents the swapchain back buffer associated with surface to the windowing system for display. wait_semaphores gate the start of execution; signal_semaphores are raised once execution completes, allowing downstream queues or the present engine to proceed. The primitive touches queue submission state, swapchain back-buffer state, and the platform compositor. Backend executors realize it as a (submit, present) pair on the target API. This is the fundamental frame-pacing primitive; sync interval / VRR negotiation lives in the surface card.

name: comp_gfx_swapchain_create
semantics: Creates a presentation swap chain (D3D12 IDXGISwapChain3 / Metal CAMetalLayer drawable pool / Vulkan VkSwapchainKHR / WebGPU GPUCanvasContext) bound to a platform surface. The swapchain manages image_count back-buffer images of dims pixels in the given format and color_space, presented to the surface using present_mode (immediate=tearing/no-sync; fifo=traditional vsync; fifo_relaxed=adaptive vsync that tears on late frames; mailbox=triple-buffered low-latency). usage declares how the swapchain images can be used (color_attachment for rendering, transfer_dst for direct copy, sampled for post-process feedback). alpha_compositing controls how the swapchain composites against the OS compositor (opaque on game windows; premultiplied/unmultiplied for transparent surfaces; inherit defers to the surface). The result is an immutable handle whose back-buffer images are acquired via a sibling primitive (deferred — comp_gfx_swapchain_acquire_next_image) and presented via comp_gfx_submit_and_present. The primitive touches device swap-chain state and platform compositor / windowing state. Backend executors realize it on the target API.

name: comp_io_buffered_line_iter
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Python 'for line in f', Ruby IO#each_line, std::getline, Rust BufRead::lines, NSString line enumeration, .NET StreamReader.ReadLine all decompose to this primitive. Promoting line iteration to a first-class IR primitive lets the substrate carry encoding and terminator policy in the type rather than in ad-hoc per-language config.
semantics: Wrap the byte stream in a buffered text iterator that yields one logical line per step, stripping the terminator. The iterator owns a buffer sized by backend policy (typically 4 KiB - 64 KiB) and refills it lazily from comp_io_stream_read. Encoding selects how raw bytes become characters; line_ending selects which sequences terminate a line ('any' accepts LF, CRLF, or bare CR). Iteration ends when the underlying stream reaches EOF; a final partial line (no terminator) is yielded if non-empty. The iterator borrows the stream_token: invoking other primitives on the underlying stream while iteration is active is a categorical error. The primitive is text-only: invoking it on a binary stream is permitted but the returned strings may contain replacement characters where the encoding could not decode.
signature: (stream: stream_token, encoding: enum{utf8,latin1,utf16le,utf16be,ascii}, line_ending: enum{lf,crlf,cr,any}) -> iterator<string>

name: comp_io_stream_close
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. fclose, std::ifstream::close, close, CloseHandle, NSStream.close, Rust drop-on-File all decompose to this primitive. Closing as a first-class IR operation lets liveness analysis track stream lifetimes and warn on leaks at compile time rather than at runtime.
semantics: Release the resources backing the stream: flush pending writes from userspace buffers, surrender the file descriptor / handle to the kernel, and invalidate the stream_token. After this call returns, the token is unusable: subsequent reads, writes, seeks, or closes through the same token are a categorical error. The primitive does not guarantee that bytes have been durably persisted to non-volatile storage (use a separate fsync-equivalent primitive for that). On error during the flush phase the close still completes (the underlying handle is released regardless) but an error is surfaced via the return channel.

name: comp_io_stream_read
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. fread, std::istream::read, recv, NSInputStream.read, Rust Read::read, ReadFile all decompose to this primitive. Treating files, sockets, and pipes uniformly at the IR level lets transport-agnostic protocols (HTTP, line-oriented parsers) be expressed once.
semantics: Read up to 'count' bytes from the stream referred to by stream_token into the buffer at ptr_token, returning the number of bytes actually transferred (0 indicates end-of-stream for a stream that supports EOF; a value less than count indicates a short read, which is normal for non-regular streams). The stream abstraction unifies file, socket, pipe, and tty: the backend selects the appropriate syscall based on the stream_token's kind. The call may block by default; non-blocking semantics are negotiated at stream-open time via a separate flag on the stream_token. Reading past EOF on a seekable stream returns 0 without error; reading from a closed stream raises invalid_stream_token.

name: comp_io_stream_seek
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. fseek, std::istream::seekg, lseek, SetFilePointerEx, NSFileHandle.seek all decompose to this primitive. Carrying seekability in the stream_token's type lets the IR refuse nonsensical seeks on pipes at validation time rather than at runtime.
semantics: Reposition the read/write cursor of the stream. The new cursor position is computed as (offset + base), where base is 0 for 'begin', the current position for 'current', and the stream length for 'end'. Returns the resulting absolute position. The primitive is defined ONLY on seekable streams: invoking it on a pipe, socket, tty, or any other non-seekable stream is a categorical error rejected at IR-typed-validation if the stream_token's seekable bit is known statically, or at runtime via the not_seekable refusal otherwise. Seeking past the current end of a writable file is permitted on POSIX (creates a sparse hole when next written); the substrate forwards this semantics to backends that support it and refuses on those that do not.
signature: (stream: stream_token, offset: i64, whence: enum{begin,current,end}) -> u64

name: comp_mem_heap_allocate
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. malloc / new / std::allocator::allocate / HeapAlloc / NSAllocateObject / Box::new all decompose to this primitive. The card-native runtime treats heap allocation as a single IR-level operation whose backend implementation can vary across allocators without changing higher-level programs.
semantics: Reserve a region of at least 'size' bytes from the process heap, aligned to at least 'alignment' bytes (which must be a power of two), and return an opaque ptr_token referring to the allocation. The returned token is the only legal handle for subsequent load/store and free operations on this allocation. The substrate does not specify the underlying allocator's free-list structure, fragmentation policy, or whether the allocation is satisfied via brk(2), mmap(2), VirtualAlloc, or a userspace pool: those are the backend executor's choice. The token is non-forgeable at the IR level; backends track the underlying virtual-address range and lifetime. The allocation is uninitialised (contents indeterminate) unless the backend supplies a calloc-style variant.

name: comp_mem_heap_free
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. free / delete / std::allocator::deallocate / HeapFree / Box::drop all decompose to this primitive. Paired with comp_mem_heap_allocate to express the malloc/free lifetime contract at IR level.
semantics: Release the heap allocation previously returned by comp_mem_heap_allocate. After this call, the ptr_token is invalid: subsequent loads, stores, or frees through the same token are undefined behaviour at the IR level (backends may detect double-free via allocator metadata but are not required to). The backend reclaims the underlying virtual-address range to the heap, which may or may not be returned to the kernel depending on allocator policy. Passing a token not produced by comp_mem_heap_allocate (e.g. a stack token or an mmap token) is a categorical error and must be refused by typed-IR validation before the primitive is invoked.

name: comp_mem_load_store
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. C *p, C++ p->field, Rust unsafe deref, struct field access, array indexing all decompose to this primitive. Carrying the type at the IR level (rather than treating memory as untyped bytes) makes alignment, ASAN-style red-zoning, and type-confusion detection first-class substrate concerns.
semantics: Typed load or store through a ptr_token at a byte offset. For 'load': read sizeof(ty) bytes at (ptr+offset), interpret as ty, and return the scalar. For 'store': interpret 'value' as ty, write sizeof(ty) bytes at (ptr+offset), and return unit. The substrate enforces that (ptr+offset, sizeof(ty)) lies within the bounds tracked for the originating allocation: out-of-bounds is a categorical IR-level error, not undefined behaviour. Alignment requirements depend on ty and target: misaligned access raises an error unless the backend declares unaligned-access support. The primitive does not specify atomicity (use the concurrency category for atomic load/store); ordering is sequenced-before within a thread but unordered with respect to other threads.
signature: (ptr: ptr_token, offset: i64, ty: type_token, op: enum{load,store}, value?: scalar) -> scalar | unit

name: comp_mem_page_protect
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. mprotect / VirtualProtect / mach_vm_protect / JIT page-toggling all decompose here. This is the IR-level locus where iOS W^X visibility is enforced (L65), preventing every JIT/WASM/dynamic-translation engine from silently violating the sandbox.
semantics: Change the page-protection bits of the virtual-address range [ptr, ptr+length) to the requested combination of readable / writable / executable. The address and length must be page-aligned (the backend rounds outward and reports the actual rounded range via an out-of-band log channel if it differs). The substrate forbids simultaneous write+exec at IR level on platforms whose policy refuses W^X: this is not merely a runtime error code but a typed-IR invariant. Successful execution returns unit; refusal raises a categorical refusal_code that the caller must handle. The protection change applies to the underlying physical mapping (or all of its aliases on platforms supporting them).
signature: (ptr: ptr_token, length: u64, protection: bitmask{read,write,exec}) -> unit

name: comp_mem_stack_alloca
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. alloca / VLAs / __builtin_alloca / C++ stack objects / Rust let-bindings on the stack all decompose to this primitive. Exposing scope-bound allocation as a first-class IR operation lets escape analysis run at the substrate level rather than per-language.
semantics: Allocate 'size' bytes on the current call frame's stack with the requested alignment and return an opaque ptr_token whose lifetime is bounded by the enclosing lexical scope (or the enclosing function frame, depending on the producer's scope discipline). The token becomes invalid the moment its owning frame is unwound (function return, exception unwind, longjmp), and the substrate must refuse any cross-frame escape: returning a stack ptr_token from its owning function is a categorical error rejected by IR validation. Stack allocation is O(1) (a single SP adjustment) and never fails for normal sizes; oversized allocations trigger stack-overflow detection at the backend's guard-page boundary.

name: comp_net_tls_handshake
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. TLS 1.3 handshake (RFC 8446) is the foundational secure-channel-setup primitive that underlies HTTPS, secure DNS, secure email, and SMTPS. This card supplies the substrate-level form.
semantics: Perform a TLS 1.3 handshake (RFC 8446; fallback TLS 1.2 RFC 5246 only if options.allow_tls_1_2) over the already-connected TCP socket_token, presenting the SNI hostname and the ALPN protocol list, validating the peer certificate chain against trust_anchors. On success returns an opaque tls_session_token usable by comp_net_tls_send_recv. The session token captures the negotiated cipher suite, the chosen ALPN protocol, the verified peer identity, and the handshake-derived traffic keys. Mutual TLS (client certificate) is selected via options.client_certificate. The primitive is target-agnostic: it describes the WHAT of TLS session establishment; the HOW (OpenSSL vs BoringSSL vs Secure Transport vs SChannel vs rustls, session resumption via PSK, 0-RTT enable) is the backend executor's responsibility.

name: comp_net_tls_send_recv
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. comp_net_tls_handshake establishes the session; this card carries the bidirectional application data over it. RFC 8446 §6 specifies the record layer and alert protocol.
semantics: Send or receive application data over an established TLS session, or initiate a half-close. The op discriminator selects send (write up to len(buffer) bytes), recv (read up to max_bytes into buffer, returning bytes_transferred), or half_close (send TLS close_notify alert in one direction). The primitive handles TLS record framing, padding, and re-keying internally. On peer close_notify the eof_observed flag is set on the recv path; on local close the session_terminated flag is set after subsequent operations. The primitive is target-agnostic: it describes the WHAT of TLS-layer I/O; the HOW (SSL_read/SSL_write loop, rustls IOState pump, Network.framework continuation, kqueue/epoll integration) is the backend executor's responsibility.
signature: (session: tls_session_token, op: enum{send, recv, half_close}, buffer: byte_sequence, max_bytes: int) -> tls_io_result{bytes_transferred, eof_observed, session_terminated}

name: comp_sys_env_var_get_set
rationale: L23-driven primitive populating the os_syscall category. getenv/setenv/environ on POSIX, GetEnvironmentVariable on Win32, NSProcessInfo.environment on Apple, std::env::var on Rust, os.environ on Python — all decompose here. Environment-variable manipulation is the canonical way games and tools discover platform paths (HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, APPDATA, TMPDIR), toggle behavior (MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE, DXVK_HUD, METAL_DEBUG_ERROR_MODE), and read CLI-passed configuration. Without a primitive, the substrate cannot express any of those paths.
semantics: Unified read/write/unset interface against the calling process's environment block. op=get returns the value bound to name, or none if unbound. op=set binds value to name in the process environment; if name already exists, the value is replaced. op=unset removes name from the environment if present (no-op if absent). op=list_keys returns the list of all currently-bound variable names. Variable values are byte strings on POSIX and wide-char strings on Win32; the substrate canonicalizes both to UTF-8. Environment writes affect only the calling process and any subsequently forked children — they do not propagate to the parent shell. Concurrent access by multiple threads is racy on POSIX (getenv/setenv are not thread-safe per the spec); the substrate's backend serializes access via a process-wide mutex. The primitive touches process environment-block state. Backend executors realize each op against the target OS API.
signature: (op: enum{get,set,unset,list_keys}, name: string|none, value: string|none) -> string | list[string] | none

name: comp_sys_file_read
rationale: L23-driven primitive populating the os_syscall category. Every read-style call from libc (fread, getline), Win32 (ReadFile, ReadFileEx), Foundation (NSFileHandle.readData), and Cocoa (FileHandle.readData) decomposes to this primitive. semantics: Read up to count bytes from the open-file-table entry identified by fd_token. If offset is the literal token "current" the read advances the file-position pointer associated with the descriptor; if offset is a u64 the read is positional and does not move the file-position pointer (analogous to pread). The returned bytes value carries an actual-count field that may be smaller than the requested count at end-of-file or short-read conditions. The primitive does not specify buffering or readahead: that is a backend optimization choice. Reading from a write-only descriptor is an error. The primitive is target-agnostic; the backend chooses which kernel entry-point honors the (count, offset) tuple.

name: comp_sys_memory_map
rationale: L23-driven primitive populating the os_syscall category. mmap, VirtualAlloc, mach_vm_allocate, malloc-via-mmap-fast-path all decompose here. This primitive is the IR-level locus where the iOS W^X constraint becomes visible to every JIT, every WASM runtime, every dynamic-translation engine — and where the substrate honestly refuses rather than silently corrupting via Proton-style work-arounds.
semantics: Reserve a region of the calling process's virtual address space of at least size bytes, with the requested protection bits and sharing flags, and return an opaque ptr_token referring to the mapping. The protection bitmask selects readability, writability, and executability independently; the flags bitmask selects shared-vs-private and anonymous-vs-file-backed semantics (file-backed mappings require a separate higher-level card that supplies the fd_token). The substrate refuses simultaneous write+exec on iOS unless the process holds the JIT entitlement: this is not a backend quirk but a documented IR-level constraint. The returned ptr_token is opaque; the backend tracks the underlying virtual-address range and is responsible for alignment to the kernel page size.
signature: (size: u64, protection: bitmask{read,write,exec}, flags: bitmask{shared,private,anonymous}) -> ptr_token

semantics: Release the virtual-memory mapping identified by ptr_token. For file-backed shared mappings the backend ensures dirty pages are written back per the host kernel's policy before the address range is unmapped. The primitive does not promise that the released address range will be reusable by a subsequent map — that is a backend address-space-management concern. name: comp_sys_signal_handler
rationale: L23-driven primitive populating the os_syscall category. signal(2)/sigaction(2) on POSIX, SetConsoleCtrlHandler/AddVectoredExceptionHandler on Win32, NSSetUncaughtExceptionHandler / signal(2) on Apple — all decompose here. Game-engine substrates need this for: (1) graceful Ctrl+C / window-close handling that flushes save data; (2) crash reporters that catch SEGV before the OS terminates the process; (3) hot-reload trigger via SIGUSR1; (4) SIGPIPE suppression on broken-socket writes so a closed network peer does not kill the process.
semantics: Single-primitive interface for asynchronous-signal handling. op=install registers handler as the action for signal; the previous handler (if any) is returned so the caller can chain. op=uninstall restores the default disposition (SIG_DFL) for signal. op=raise synthesizes signal in the calling process (mostly used for testing and for graceful abort paths). op=block prevents signal from being delivered until op=unblock is invoked; the OS holds the signal in the pending set. op=query returns the currently-installed handler reference without modification. signal is a canonical enum that the substrate maps to platform-specific signal numbers (POSIX SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2/SIGPIPE/SIGABRT/SIGSEGV/SIGBUS/SIGFPE/SIGILL/SIGQUIT/SIGWINCH/SIGCHLD on Linux/Darwin; Win32 console-control handler events CTRL_C_EVENT/CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT via SetConsoleCtrlHandler; structured exceptions like SEGV/BUS/FPE/ILL via Win32 vectored-exception-handler when AddVectoredExceptionHandler is enabled). custom_app_signal is a substrate-internal signal slot mapped to SIGUSR1+offset / Win32 user-defined events. flags carries SA_RESTART (auto-restart interrupted syscalls), SA_NOCLDWAIT, SA_SIGINFO (extended siginfo_t to handler), SA_ONSTACK (use signal stack). semantics: Suspend the calling thread for at least duration_ms milliseconds. name: comp_persist_transaction_begin
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. SQLite BEGIN, LMDB mdb_txn_begin, RocksDB Transaction, JDBC Connection.setAutoCommit(false), Core Data performAndWait all decompose to this primitive. Promoting isolation to a typed enum lets the IR refuse engine/isolation mismatches before any data is touched.
semantics: Open a durable transaction against the store and return a txn_token that must be supplied to subsequent put/get/delete primitives invoked under the transaction. 'mode' selects whether the transaction may issue writes; 'isolation' selects the engine's visibility policy: 'snapshot' (the transaction sees a consistent snapshot from begin-time), 'serializable' (the engine refuses concurrent commits that would violate one-shot serializability), 'read_committed' (each read sees the latest committed value, which may shift between reads). Not all engines support all isolation levels: the primitive refuses with categorical error if the engine cannot honour the requested level, rather than silently degrading. Holding a txn_token consumes engine resources (a WAL slot, a snapshot reference); the substrate refuses unbounded held transactions per backend policy.

name: comp_persist_transaction_commit
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. SQLite COMMIT/ROLLBACK, LMDB mdb_txn_commit, RocksDB Transaction::Commit, JDBC Connection.commit/rollback, Core Data save/rollback all decompose to this primitive. Unifying commit and rollback under a single primitive with a typed action lets liveness analysis prove that every txn_token is eventually concluded.
semantics: Conclude the transaction referred to by txn_token. With action='commit' the engine attempts to make the transaction's writes durably visible: under snapshot or serializable isolation this may fail with commit_conflict if another transaction has committed an incompatible change since this transaction's snapshot, in which case the caller must retry. With action='rollback' the transaction's writes are discarded and the call cannot fail (modulo IO errors flushing the WAL header). In both cases the txn_token is invalidated; subsequent operations on it are a categorical error. The durability of a successful commit is fsynced by default: this primitive defines the durability boundary for the substrate's persistence model.

rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. handle_release is the dual of handle_acquire and the foundation of leak-freedom proofs; lowering of using/defer/RAII cards bottoms out here.
semantics: Release a resource handle, returning any kernel- or runtime-allocated structures, decrementing reference counts, and removing the handle from the per-process handle table. After release the handle is invalid; subsequent uses must trap (use-after-release is a substrate-detectable error). Releases must be exactly-once: double-release on the same handle is undefined under POSIX (may close an unrelated fd reopened in the meantime) and explicitly invalid under Windows. The primitive pairs with comp_res_handle_acquire under linear-typing discipline; static analysis cards check the pairing.

name: comp_res_lease_request
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Lease primitives are the substrate beneath distributed locks, GPU residency, and graceful degradation; modeling leases as first-class lets self-healing cards compose against expiry semantics directly.
semantics: Acquire a time-bounded reservation of a resource. The lease auto-expires at expires_at if not explicitly renewed; on expiry the underlying resource is reclaimed by the issuing authority without consulting the holder. Leases generalize file locks, distributed locks, GPU memory residency tickets, and rate-limit tokens. The holder must renew before TTL elapses or surrender via comp_res_handle_release; the substrate guarantees the lease is observable but does not freeze wall-clock to align renewal windows. Lease semantics give the substrate a model for self-healing resource pools and Chubby/Etcd-style coordination.

name: comp_res_lifetime_attach
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. lifetime_attach is the substrate primitive behind RAII, with-statements, defer, and structured-concurrency cancellation propagation; it is the linchpin between resource and control_flow categories.
semantics: Bind a resource handle to a lifetime context such that the substrate releases the handle automatically when the context exits. Lifetime contexts compose: nested scopes form a stack and exit in LIFO order. The primitive is the substrate equivalent of Rust drop-on-scope-exit, C++ destructor cascade, and Python __exit__ chains. Attaching the same handle to multiple scopes is rejected (linear typing); detaching and re-attaching is permitted under explicit caller action. The lifetime context itself is created and destroyed by separate scope-management primitives in the control_flow category.

name: comp_shader_arithmetic
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #6 of 11. Vector arithmetic is the densest opcode bucket in every shader; modeling it as one parametric primitive collapses the per-language operator tables into a single dispatch and lets backends emit native operators directly.
semantics: Component-wise vector arithmetic across scalar and vec2/vec3/vec4/matNxM operands. Binary ops (add, sub, mul, div, min, max, mod, rem) take two args of compatible shape; unary ops (abs, sign, neg) take one. Operand types follow shader-language broadcasting rules: scalar+vec promotes the scalar to a same-width vec; vec*matrix is row-vector times matrix; matrix*matrix is standard matrix multiply (this primitive's 'mul' op carries no per-component-vs-matrix-product ambiguity because the dispatch is on the args' types). Floating-point arithmetic is IEEE-754 with the implementation-defined rounding mode the target GPU uses (typically round-to-nearest-even); integer overflow wraps modulo-2^N like every shader language.

name: comp_shader_atomic_op
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive added as gap-closure. Modern GPU-driven rendering (Nanite-style geometry, GPU-driven culling, indirect-multi-draw, parallel BVH traversal, lock-free hashing) depends on first-class atomics with explicit memory ordering and scope — the existing comp_shader_storage_buffer_rw atomic sub-ops are sufficient for hello-world cases but lack the memory_order + scope parameterization required for lock-free correctness across waves and across dispatches. Separating atomics into their own primitive lets the substrate emit the most direct intrinsic per backend and validate per-target capability tiers (int64-atomics, float-atomics).
semantics: Performs an atomic read-modify-write at index in the storage / structured / shared buffer at binding slot. Unlike comp_shader_storage_buffer_rw (which also exposes atomics as a sub-op), this primitive is the canonical atomic-only surface with explicit memory_order and scope parameters — required for high-performance lock-free GPU data structures (concurrent hash maps, parallel BVH refits, indirect-draw counters, work-stealing queues, GPU-driven LOD streaming). atomic_add/sub/min/max/and/or/xor/exchange perform the named operation and return the pre-modification value. atomic_compare_exchange compares the slot to compare_value and replaces with value only if equal; returns the actual pre-modification value (caller compares to determine success). atomic_load / atomic_store are memory-fenced loads/stores. atomic_fetch_inc / atomic_fetch_dec are the canonical counter-increment idioms. type selects the per-element type — int32/uint32 are universally supported, int64/uint64 require shader-model-6.6+ on D3D / VK_KHR_shader_atomic_int64 on Vulkan / Metal 2.4+, float32/float64 require SM6.6+ / SPV_EXT_shader_atomic_float / Metal 3.0+. scope is the visibility horizon: device atomics are visible to all dispatches in the queue, workgroup atomics are visible only within the thread group (typically backed by groupshared / threadgroup / Workgroup-storage memory), subgroup atomics scope to the wave / simdgroup. memory_order follows the C11/C++11 atomics model and translates to the target's barrier semantics.

name: comp_shader_branch
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #8 of 11. Branching inside shaders is universal but its cost model is target-specific (lane-mask predication vs hardware branch); centralizing the primitive while declaring per-target lane assumptions lets the substrate's backends pick the right emit form per GPU.
semantics: An if/else conditional inside a shader. The condition is a per-lane boolean (or a per-lane bool-vector reduced to bool by an explicit any/all). When condition is uniform across the wave/subgroup, the branch is taken or skipped wave-wide (fast). When condition is divergent (some lanes true, some false), GPUs either mask off the inactive lanes (executing both sides with predication, slow) or actually re-converge — the choice is hardware-specific. Side effects inside each body are valid; the cards inside true_body / false_body execute in lane-mask order. The primitive does not specify uniform vs. divergent at the IR level; backends infer or honor a separate uniformity hint when one is available (HLSL [branch] / [flatten], SPIR-V SelectionControl flags).

per_target_lane_assumptions.amd_wave32_or_wave64: 32 lanes (RDNA) or 64 lanes (GCN); wider waves amplify divergence cost proportionally
per_target_lane_assumptions.android_potential_varied: Mali and PowerVR have their own wave / quad notions; no single lane count assumption is portable
per_target_lane_assumptions.apple_simdgroup_32_lanes: 32 lanes per simdgroup on Apple7+; pre-Apple7 iPads may have different widths; reconvergence behavior differs from D3D wave model
per_target_lane_assumptions.intel_xe_simd16_or_simd32: 16 or 32 lanes depending on shader compilation choice; can vary per-shader
per_target_lane_assumptions.nvidia_warp_32_lanes: 32 lanes per warp; divergent branches use per-thread predication via SIMT execution mask
per_target_lane_assumptions.qualcomm_wave_size_64_or_128: Adreno wave can be 64 or 128 wide depending on shader; mobile divergence cost scales accordingly

uniformity_handling.divergent_branch_predicated_path: When the condition varies per lane, GPUs execute both sides with execution-mask predication: cost is sum-of-both-sides, plus a mask reconvergence at the join. This is the worst case on every architecture.
uniformity_handling.hlsl_hint_branch_vs_flatten: HLSL [branch] forces a real branch; [flatten] forces predication (both sides executed). The substrate's IR carries neither; consumers can attach a uniformity_hint to choose.
uniformity_handling.spirv_selection_control: SPIR-V OpSelectionMerge takes a SelectionControl mask (None | Flatten | DontFlatten); backends emit Flatten when consumer requests predication.
uniformity_handling.uniform_branch_optimal_path: When the substrate proves all lanes share the condition (e.g. condition is a uniform-buffer-derived scalar), the backend emits a hardware branch with no per-lane masking — same cost as a CPU branch.

name: comp_shader_fragment_output_store
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #5 of 11. Fragment output is where a shader actually changes the framebuffer; modeling it as a primitive lets the substrate uniformly handle HLSL SV_TARGET / MSL [[color(N)]] / SPIR-V Output / GLSL layout(location) without external translation.
semantics: Write a 4-component color value to the fragment shader output at the given render-target index. The output_location selects which color attachment (0..N) receives the value; the depth output is a sibling case with location='depth'. Per-fragment blending, write-masking, and alpha-to-coverage are governed by host pipeline state, not by this primitive: the primitive only declares the per-shader-invocation value to deposit. Calling this primitive twice with the same output_location within a single fragment invocation is undefined-behavior territory (HLSL allows it as the last write; MSL forbids it in strict mode). Multi-render-target writes are expressed as multiple invocations of this primitive with distinct locations.

semantics: A built-in shader function dispatched by intrinsic enum. name: comp_shader_loop
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #9 of 11. Loops are the second pillar of shader control flow after branches; modeling them as a primitive lets the substrate handle HLSL [unroll(N)] / SPIR-V LoopMerge / MSL native loops uniformly.
semantics: A for / while loop inside a shader. init (optional) initializes a per-lane loop variable; cond evaluates to a per-lane bool each iteration; if true, body executes and advance (optional) updates the loop variable; if false, control exits to the next IR node. The loop may carry an attribute hint for full unrolling, partial unrolling, or no unrolling (HLSL [unroll(N)] / [loop]; SPIR-V LoopControl Unroll / DontUnroll / PartialCount). Bounded loops with compile-time-known trip counts are commonly fully unrolled by every shader compiler regardless of hint; runtime-bounded loops are kept as loops. Wave-divergent loops (different lanes exit at different iterations) execute until the last active lane exits; inactive lanes are masked out — same execution-mask model as comp_shader_branch.

name: comp_shader_ray_trace
rationale: Card-native shader IR gap-closure: ray tracing is the most prominent post-2018 GPU primitive that the substrate did not yet model. Modern AAA titles (Cyberpunk 2077, Alan Wake 2, Path of Exile 2, the Indiana Jones engine, Elden Ring's potential RT path on iPad M-series) emit DXR TraceRay and Vulkan RayQuery instructions whose card-native equivalents must exist for the redefinition graph to remain complete. Inline RT (RayQuery) is now broadly supported on Apple Silicon (A13+), all RTX cards, all RDNA2+ AMD cards, and Intel Arc — substrate compiles the same comp_shader_ray_trace primitive to the appropriate per-target intrinsic.
semantics: Ray-tracing intrinsic. Two sub-models: (1) classic pipeline-RT — op=trace_ray issues a ray against the bound acceleration structure; the GPU walks the BVH, runs intersection/any-hit shaders, and writes the closest-hit / miss result into payload; op=report_hit is called from inside intersection shaders to report a custom-geometry intersection at the given hit_kind; op=call_shader invokes a callable-shader by SBT index. (2) inline (RayQuery) — op=trace_ray_inline_begin opens a ray-query against the accel structure with the given ray; op=trace_ray_inline_proceed advances the traversal one step and returns whether any candidate is available; the shader may inspect candidates and decide to op=trace_ray_inline_commit (accept) or op=trace_ray_inline_abandon (skip); op=trace_ray_inline_get_committed reads the final committed intersection. ray_flags carries: opaque/no_opaque to skip any-hit, cull_back_face/cull_front_face, cull_opaque/cull_non_opaque, accept_first_hit_and_end_search (early-out), skip_triangles/skip_aabbs (geometry filtering), force_opaque. instance_mask is logically ANDed with each instance's mask in the TLAS — zero means skip. accel_struct_binding refers to a top-level acceleration structure resource bound via the descriptor table (comp_gfx_descriptor_table_layout with kind=acceleration_structure). The primitive is hardware-gated: classic RT requires DXR Tier 1.1 / VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline / MTLAccelerationStructure (Apple 6+ hardware support); inline RT is more broadly available (DXR 1.1 on most cards, RayQuery on Vulkan, MTLAccelerationStructure ray queries on Apple Silicon).

name: comp_shader_storage_buffer_rw
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #3 of 11. Storage buffer R/W and atomic ops are the substrate of compute shaders and modern indirect-draw / GPU-driven rendering. A target-agnostic primitive lets the substrate model RWStructuredBuffer / device pointers / SSBOs uniformly.
semantics: Read, write, or atomically modify an element at the given index of a mutable storage / structured buffer (HLSL RWStructuredBuffer / RWBuffer, GLSL buffer block, SPIR-V StorageBuffer, MSL device pointer). The op enum selects: load (returns value, no side effect on this lane alone), store (writes value, returns none), or atomic-* (returns the pre-modification value, performs the modification with atomic semantics across all lanes and dispatches). Atomic ops on float types require target capability (HLSL SM6.6+, Metal 3.0+, SPV_EXT_shader_atomic_float); on integer types they are universally supported. The buffer is bound at slot 'binding'; the element type is determined by the buffer's declared struct; bounds are checked only if the target's robust-buffer-access feature is enabled.

name: comp_shader_struct_compose
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #11 of 11. Struct and vector composition is the universal value-assembly operation; modeling it as a single primitive collapses HLSL's float4(...) / MSL's float4(...) / SPIR-V's OpCompositeConstruct / GLSL's vec4(...) into one card.
semantics: Assemble a struct or vector value from a list of (name, value) member pairs. When all member names are positional ('x', 'y', 'z', 'w' or anonymous), the result is a vector of the corresponding width: float4(x, y, z, w) is comp_shader_struct_compose([('x', x), ('y', y), ('z', z), ('w', w)]). When names match a named struct's field list, the result is that struct value. Used for: vector constructor calls (float4(...)), struct returns from functions, and assembling vertex-output / fragment-input records in shaders that don't use the per-field SV_/[[attribute]] style. The primitive is pure: composing fields produces a value with no side effect.

name: comp_shader_texture_sample
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #2 of 11. Texture sampling is the dominant per-pixel cost in any renderer that uses materials; without a target-agnostic primitive, every texture op chains through HLSL -> DXBC -> SPIR-V -> MSL. This card lets the substrate's backends emit native sampling per target.
semantics: Sample a 2D texture at the given UV coordinate using the given sampler state, returning a 4-component RGBA value of the texture's component type (float / half / unorm-promoted-to-float). The lod argument selects the mip-level: 'auto' means implicit lod from screen-space derivatives (valid in fragment stage); a scalar means an explicit lod (valid in any stage). The texture and sampler are bound at separate slots in this IR (matching HLSL Texture/SamplerState separation and SPIR-V sampled-image vs separate-image+sampler); backends that require a combined sampler+texture handle (legacy GLSL sampler2D) compose them at emit time. The result is in the texture's logical color space; gamma decode and sRGB conversion are determined by the texture format declared by the caller, not this primitive.
signature: (texture_binding: u32, sampler_binding: u32, uv: vec2, lod: scalar | "auto") -> rgba

name: comp_shader_uniform_buffer_load
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #1 of 11. Replaces the HLSL -> DXBC/DXIL -> SPIR-V (DXVK) -> MSL (SPIRV-Cross) chain by emitting the per-target form directly from this IR. Constant-buffer access is the most common per-draw read in every renderer; centralizing it as a substrate primitive lets shader corpora be reasoned about and re-emitted without external translators.
semantics: Load a value of the given scalar/vector type from a uniform / constant buffer at a binding slot and byte offset. The binding selects the buffer (a per-pipeline immutable view of CPU-uploaded constants); the offset addresses a single member within the buffer's layout. The result is a target-agnostic SSA value of the requested type. The primitive does not specify packing rules (std140 / cbuffer-default / Metal argument-buffer): those are layout decisions resolved by the backend when serializing the buffer struct. Reads are pure within a draw / dispatch: a uniform buffer is immutable for the duration of the GPU work that references it.
signature: (buffer_binding: u32, field_offset_bytes: u32, type: scalar_or_vec) -> value

name: comp_shader_vertex_input_load
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #4 of 11. Vertex input is the start of the per-vertex data path; modeling it as a target-agnostic primitive lets the substrate match HLSL semantic names, MSL [[attribute]], SPIR-V Location, and GLSL layout(location) to a single canonical slot index per shader.
semantics: Load a per-vertex attribute (position, normal, UV, color, tangent, blend-weight, etc.) at the given attribute location, returning a value of the declared vector or scalar type. The location is the IR-level slot index that backends bind to: HLSL semantic strings (POSITION, NORMAL, TEXCOORD0) are resolved into numeric slots at emit time; MSL [[attribute(N)]] uses N directly; SPIR-V uses OpDecorate Location N on an Input variable. The attribute's binary representation (interleaved vs. non-interleaved buffer layout, normalized integer vs. float) is declared by the host pipeline state, not this primitive. A vertex shader's input set is the union of all comp_shader_vertex_input_load locations it references.

name: comp_shader_wave_op
rationale: Card-native shader IR primitive #10 of 11. Wave / subgroup / simdgroup ops are the densest cross-target gotcha in shader translation: every API exposes them with different names, different lane counts, and different uniformity guarantees. Centralizing them as a single parametric primitive with explicit per-target lane assumptions lets the substrate route them correctly per GPU.
semantics: Subgroup / wave / simdgroup-level collective: every active lane in the wave participates and reads a result derived from the values of all active lanes. ballot returns a per-lane bitmask of which lanes satisfied a predicate; all / any reduces the predicate across the wave; broadcast picks one lane's value and returns it to all; reduce_* combines all lanes via the named operator; exclusive_scan_* / inclusive_scan_* return per-lane prefix sums; shuffle_* exchanges values between lanes by lane index or xor pattern; quad_* operates on a 2x2 quad of fragment lanes. The 'wave' / 'subgroup' / 'simdgroup' is a hardware-defined group of co-executing lanes; the abstract semantic of every op is target-agnostic but the concrete lane count and execution-mask handling differ per GPU and per target API — see target_aware_semantics.

lane_count_per_target.amd_gcn_legacy: 64 lanes per wave; algorithms hardcoded to 32 lanes break here
lane_count_per_target.amd_rdna_default: 32 lanes per wave by default; can be 64 via shader compilation flag
lane_count_per_target.android_potential_mali_powervr: Mali GPUs have 4 / 8 / 16 lane 'quads'; PowerVR has its own model; portability requires runtime queries
lane_count_per_target.apple_apple7_plus: 32 lanes per simdgroup on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3 + A14+ phones / iPads)
lane_count_per_target.apple_pre_apple7: different simdgroup widths (16 or 32 depending on family)
lane_count_per_target.intel_xe_simd16_or_32: 16 or 32 lanes; backend selects based on register pressure
lane_count_per_target.nvidia_blackwell_plus: 32 lanes per warp (unchanged); thread blocks still 32-wide
lane_count_per_target.nvidia_pre_blackwell: 32 lanes per warp; HLSL WaveGetLaneCount() returns 32; SPIR-V SubgroupSize is 32
lane_count_per_target.qualcomm_adreno: wave can be 64 or 128 wide depending on shader and chip family

uniformity_assumptions.active_mask_dependent: every wave op reads from the set of CURRENTLY ACTIVE lanes (not the original launch set); if the surrounding control flow has masked some lanes off via a divergent if/loop, the wave op only sees the unmasked subset — this is the single biggest source of cross-target bugs because divergent execution mask handling differs in subtle ways between HLSL DXIL, MSL, and SPIR-V
uniformity_assumptions.hlsl_dxil_active_lane_semantics: HLSL SM6.0+ WaveActive* explicitly operate on currently-active lanes; WaveReadLaneAt(value, laneIdx) requires laneIdx to be an active lane else the result is undefined
uniformity_assumptions.msl_simd_active_lane_semantics: MSL simd_* functions also operate on active simd lanes; the simdgroup_size is queryable at runtime via [[threads_per_simdgroup]]
uniformity_assumptions.spirv_subgroup_active_lane_semantics: SPIR-V OpGroupNonUniform* with the Subgroup scope operate on active subgroup invocations; the Workgroup scope is a different beast spanning the whole compute workgroup
uniformity_assumptions.wave_ops_inside_divergent_control_flow_u: SM6.0 originally forbade wave ops inside divergent if/else; SM6.5 (WaveSize attribute) and later relaxed this with explicit semantics; older drivers may still produce undefined behavior

rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Expansion is the dual of factorization and the precondition for many symbolic identity checks; the substrate's universal solver needs a card-native expansion to compare canonical forms without dropping to sympy.
semantics: Distribute products over sums and apply binomial-style expansions until the expression is in sum-of-products normal form. name: comp_sym_finite_field_op
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Finite-field arithmetic is the substrate of elliptic-curve cryptography, BCH/Reed-Solomon coding, and polynomial factorization (Berlekamp). Making GF(p^n) card-native unblocks cards in cards/computation/verification/ and cards/security/* from a galois PyPI dependency.
semantics: Arithmetic in the finite field GF(p^n). For n=1: ordinary modular arithmetic mod p. For n>1: arithmetic in the polynomial ring Z_p[x] / (m(x)) where m is an irreducible degree-n polynomial over Z_p, with elements represented as degree-<n polynomials with coefficients in {0..p-1}. op selects add (componentwise mod p), mul (polynomial mul then reduce mod m), div (mul by inv), neg (componentwise additive inverse), inv (extended Euclidean over Z_p[x]). div/inv are undefined for the zero element.

name: comp_type_check_subtype
rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Subtype checking is the substrate's mechanism for safe assignment, function-argument acceptance, and Liskov substitution; every type-aware card (lowering, mapping, redefinition) consults this primitive.
semantics: Decide whether sub is a subtype of sup, i.e. whether every inhabitant of sub is also an inhabitant of sup. The relation is reflexive (T <: T) and transitive (T <: U and U <: V implies T <: V). Per-constructor rules: int subtype follows representation-inclusion (i8 <: i16 <: i32 <: i64 for signed widenings); function subtyping is contravariant-in-domain, covariant-in-codomain (per Pierce TAPL ch. 15); record subtyping is width + depth; sum subtyping is dual to records. The check is decidable for the simply-typed and bounded-polymorphic fragments; full F-sub is undecidable and the substrate's checker is a sound under-approximation.

rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. Records are the canonical product type; serialization, RPC argument bundles, and config schemas all bottom out into this card.

rationale: L23-driven W47 substrate population. The verification category was deferred; this primitive populates it with the minimal runtime-assertion contract.
